scoring.compression: 1=minimal boilerplate reduction, 5=one DSL declaration can replace a subsystem
scoring.semantic_overhead: 1=already-native/easy for Astra to infer, 5=new opaque semantic dialect
scoring.production_readiness: high=widely deployed/currently maintained; medium=credible but narrower/unstable; experimental=not default architecture

policy.external_dependency_gate: adopt only when recurring generated-code/token savings exceed new semantic surface
policy.expansion_rule: metaprogramming that creates methods/routes/policies/UI must emit or expose a machine-readable expansion/index
policy.proof_rule: no metaprogramming/process success may satisfy formal proof gates

candidates.name: Rails / ActiveSupport + ActiveModel + ActiveRecord DSLs
candidates.reason: Already the host framework and dominant GitLab vocabulary; highest compression with near-zero new review dialect.

candidates.name: GitLab DeclarativePolicy
candidates.reason: Already central to GitLab authorization; ideal for Aegis policy/RBAC without inventing another policy language.

candidates.name: Grape
candidates.reason: GitLab already uses it heavily; compact API/validation declarations can generate substantial behavior.

candidates.name: GraphQL-Ruby
candidates.reason: Already integrated into GitLab; excellent declarative density but only useful when GraphQL is actually the interface.

candidates.name: ViewComponent
candidates.reason: GitLab already uses ViewComponent/Pajamas; reduces repeated HAML/UI without adding a second frontend model.

candidates.name: Simple Form
candidates.reason: Very compact forms, but GitLab already has its own UI/form conventions; extra dependency and visual dialect likely cost more review tokens than it saves.

candidates.name: ActiveAdmin
candidates.reason: Extremely compressive but effectively introduces an admin framework inside GitLab's existing product UI, duplicating routing/auth/view semantics.

candidates.name: Administrate
candidates.reason: Closer to standard Rails than ActiveAdmin, but still duplicates GitLab's supervision UI stack and creates a second dashboard dialect.

candidates.name: dry-validation
candidates.reason: Strong declarative contracts; worthwhile only if one schema becomes the source for UI+MCP+API validation rather than a parallel contract language.

candidates.name: dry-types
candidates.reason: Some GitLab dependency graph already contains it; useful as implementation detail but not enough reason to establish a new project-wide DSL.

candidates.name: dry-schema
candidates.reason: High contract density; adopt only if it replaces multiple hand-maintained schemas and can generate review-visible expansion.

candidates.name: dry-struct
candidates.reason: Useful for data contracts but less compelling than existing Rails/GitLab objects unless a shared schema generator consumes it.

candidates.name: dry-initializer
candidates.reason: Saves boilerplate but not enough characters/files to justify a new dependency in this architecture.

candidates.name: dry-configurable
candidates.reason: Already transitive in GitLab, but Aegis host configuration should remain explicit and fail-closed rather than introduce another config layer.

candidates.name: Trailblazer
candidates.reason: Very high behavior density, but it introduces a full business-logic architecture whose review vocabulary would compete with Aegis roadmaps and Dagger.

candidates.name: state_machines
candidates.reason: Excellent density for ordinary runtime state; Aegis formalization roadmap is already machine-readable and should not be duplicated into another state-machine DSL.

candidates.name: Action Policy
candidates.reason: Good Rails authorization DSL, but GitLab already has DeclarativePolicy; adding it would duplicate the most security-sensitive semantic surface.

candidates.name: Tapioca
candidates.reason: Valuable visibility for Sorbet codebases, but project states API/interface remain pre-1.0 and GitLab is not a Tapioca/Sorbet architecture. Aegis should instead emit its own expansion manifest.

candidates.name: Ruby Next
candidates.reason: Interesting for syntax research but not a boilerplate-reduction win for pinned GitLab Rails; custom syntax would raise agent review cost.

candidates.name: Roundhouse
candidates.reason: Potentially extreme compression/translation capability but exact GitLab Rails compatibility is unproven; keep outside required runtime.
